claims.evidence: The witness sees the exterior, but internal completeness and the presence of all auxiliary components cannot be confirmed from two photos.
Photo 1 shows a label on the valve cover with 'CAT' and 'C9 ACERT'.
It is unclear if the seller means the engine is for salvage or is a complete unit being sold as a spare part.

risks.risk: The engine may be seized or have major internal mechanical failure.
risks.proof: A video of the engine being barred over manually or a cold start video.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-running core for rebuild

risks.risk: High operational hours leading to imminent failure.
risks.proof: A screenshot of an ECM diagnostic report showing total engine hours.
risks.if_unproven: as a high-hour unit at the end of its service life

risks.risk: Hidden cracks in the block or head, or significant fluid leaks.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running at operating temperature for at least 10 minutes.
risks.if_unproven: as having major leaks requiring a full gasket and seal overhaul

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and running.
ECM diagnostic printout or photo of the hour meter.
Photos of the oil pan and underside to check for leaks.
Close-up photo of the data plate showing the serial number.
response.reason: The engine model is confirmed as a CAT C9 ACERT. It can be priced at its worst-case value as a non-functional core unit for parts.
